Goal — Extended Factory State Retention & Card Lifecycle History Preservation (v1)

**The factory state publisher (`js/factoryState.js`) retains merged PR cards for 7 days (up from 24 hours), keeps up to 500 snapshot entries in `<base>-history.json` (up from 72), and preserves up to 100 per-card state transitions in `card.history` (up from 24), so the factory board (`dmtools-factory`) can render multi-day timelines, time-travel across days, and retain full card lifecycle histories without premature truncation.**

Today, `js/factoryState.js` enforces three aggressive retention caps designed only for a short 6-hour / 24-hour window:
1. `MERGED_WINDOW_MS = 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000` (24 hours): merged PRs drop out of `lanes.merged_recent` 24 hours after `merged_at`. Worse, because `prevIndex(prev)` carries forward accumulated lifecycle timestamps (`reviewedAt`, `approvedAt`, `validatingAt`) and `card.history` only for cards still present in `prev`, once a merged PR leaves `merged_recent` its accumulated lifecycle metadata is permanently lost from the rolling state.
2. `HISTORY_KEEP = 72`: `updateHistory()` writes every timestamped snapshot file `data/<base>-<stamp>.json` to the `factory-data` branch (never deleting the files), but slices the `snapshots` index in `data/<base>-history.json` to `72` entries (~6 hours at 5-minute ticks), making older snapshots unreachable from the board's time-travel slider.
3. `HISTORY_CAP = 24`: `capHistory()` slices `card.history` (`[{ state, at }, ...]`) to the last 24 transitions, truncating the earliest transitions on long-lived or multi-rework cards.

## Architecture & Constants (`js/factoryState.js`)

| Constant | Current Value | New Value | Rationale |
|----------|---------------|-----------|-----------|
| `MERGED_WINDOW_MS` | `24 * 60 * 60 * 1000` (24h) | `7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000` (7 days) | Keeps merged PR cards and their accumulated lifecycle timestamps/history in `lanes.merged_recent` for a full week |
| `HISTORY_KEEP` | `72` (~6h of 5m ticks) | `500` (~41h+ of 5m ticks) | Expands `data/<base>-history.json` index so the board time-travel slider covers multi-day history while keeping JSON payload size small (~80 KB) |
| `HISTORY_CAP` | `24` transitions | `100` transitions | Preserves full card state transition history from `issue_created` / `pr_created` through `merged` even across multiple review/rework/validation cycles |

### Invariants
- `cfg.historyKeep` override in `updateHistory(state, cfg, exec)` continues to take precedence when explicitly passed by callers/tests (`var keep = (cfg && cfg.historyKeep) || HISTORY_KEEP;`).
- `SCHEMA_VERSION` stays `2` (additive retention widening; no schema shape break).
- Existing behavior for cards outside the widened 7-day `MERGED_WINDOW_MS` remains identical (dropped cleanly with no orphan token rows).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1 — 7-day merged PR retention (`MERGED_WINDOW_MS`):** `MERGED_WINDOW_MS` is `7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000` (`604800000`). A merged PR whose `merged_at` is within 7 days of `now` (e.g. 2 days or 6 days ago) stays in `lanes.merged_recent` and preserves its `prev` lifecycle timestamps (`reviewedAt`, `approvedAt`, `validatingAt`), `card.history`, and `card.tokens`; a merged PR older than 7 days is excluded.
- **AC2 — 500-snapshot history index (`HISTORY_KEEP`):** `HISTORY_KEEP` is `500` (and exported on `module.exports` if needed for test assertions). `updateHistory()` defaults to keeping up to `500` snapshots in `<base>-history.json` when `cfg.historyKeep` is not specified, while still honoring an explicit `cfg.historyKeep` override.
- **AC3 — 100-transition card history cap (`HISTORY_CAP`):** `HISTORY_CAP` is `100`. `capHistory()` retains up to `100` `{ state, at }` transitions per card before slicing to the most recent `100`.
- **AC4 — Unit test suite updated and green:** `js/unit-tests/test_factoryState.js` (and any sibling unit tests touching `merged_recent` window or `HISTORY_CAP` / `HISTORY_KEEP`) is updated for the new bounds and passes 100%.

## Test plan

- `UT-1` (**AC1**): Verify `buildFactoryState` retains merged PRs at 48h and 6d23h inside `lanes.merged_recent` (including carry-over from `prev` and token attachment), and drops merged PRs at >7d (e.g. 8 days before `now`).
- `UT-2` (**AC2**): Verify `updateHistory` default cap retains >72 snapshots (up to 500) and slices at 500 when `cfg.historyKeep` is omitted, and still trims to `cfg.historyKeep` when explicitly provided.
- `UT-3` (**AC3**): Verify `capHistory` / `nextHistory` keeps 50 transitions intact and caps at 100 when >100 transitions are accumulated.
- `REG-1` (**AC4**): `node js/unit-tests/test_factoryState.js` passes with zero failures.

## Non-goals
- Changing token ledger window (`DEFAULT_WINDOW_DAYS = 14` / `ROW_KEEP = 40` in `js/factory/token_usage.js` and `scripts/publish-token-usage.sh`) — out of scope for this issue.
- Deleting historical `data/<base>-<stamp>.json` files from the `factory-data` branch.

search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:

Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. If pr_diff.txt is truncated, run git diff origin/{base}...HEAD to see the full diff"] ``` Example PR review outputs — keep concise: ### outputs/pr_review.json ```json { "recommendation": "BLOCK", "summary": "SQL injection in UserService.js must be fixed before merge.", "generalComment": "outputs/pr_review_general.md", "inlineComments": [ {"path":"src/auth/UserService.js","line":45,"comment":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md","severity":"BLOCKING"}, {"path":"src/auth/LoginController.js","line":78,"comment":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md","severity":"IMPORTANT"}, {"path":"src/utils/validation.js","line":23,"comment":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment3.md","severity":"SUGGESTION"} ], "issueCounts": {"blocking":1,"important":1,"suggestions":1} } ``` ### outputs/pr_review_general.md ```markdown ## Automated Code Review — BLOCK **Summary**: SQL injection blocks merge. Strengthen password validation (8+ chars, mixed case, numbers, symbols) 3. Extract shared email validation utility ``` ### outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md ```markdown 🚨 **BLOCKING: SQL Injection** User input is interpolated directly into the query at `UserService.js:45`: ```javascript const query = `SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = '${email}'`; ``` Use parameterized queries instead: ```javascript const query = 'SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = ?'; await db.query(query, [email]); ``` ``` # Review verdict rules — machine protocol (binding) The review↔rework loop is a machine, not a conversation: your `recommendation` in `outputs/pr_review.json` is parsed mechanically and drives issue labels, rework runs and CI (each wasted round costs 15–20 CI minutes — gh-71). These rules govern the verdict; every other instruction (severity definitions, output files, thread etiquette) is unchanged. ## Verdict mapping Classify findings exactly as instructed: - 🚨 **BLOCKING** — correctness/bug findings: broken behavior, failing gates (red CI), scope violations, security issues, data loss. - ⚠️ **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability debt worth fixing, but the PR works as shipped. - 💡 **SUGGESTION** — style, wording, import order, dartdoc refs, polish. Do NOT kill it mid-flight — let it finish, treat the result as stale, then deliberately start a fresh run against the updated tree"] B7["B6 covers a job still making progress — do NOT kill it mid-flight; a job with NO progress for ~10 min (or 2× its expected duration) is HUNG — dispose of it and MOVE ON: bash_job stop <job-id>, note the disposal in the deliverable (job id, command, last output tail), finish the remaining steps and write outputs/response.md reporting the unverified part. NEVER let a hung child hold the deliverable hostage: validation CI on the pull request is the safety net"] B1 --> B2 --> B3 --> B4 --> B5 --> B6 --> B7 end USE --> SHELLSTATE SHELLSTATE --> CWD CWD --> BGJOBS ``` # Review verdict rules — machine protocol (binding) The review↔rework loop is a machine, not a conversation: your `recommendation` in `outputs/pr_review.json` is parsed mechanically and drives issue labels, rework runs and CI (each wasted round costs 15–20 CI minutes — gh-71). These rules govern the verdict; every other instruction (severity definitions, output files, thread etiquette) is unchanged. ## Verdict mapping Classify findings exactly as instructed: - 🚨 **BLOCKING** — correctness/bug findings: broken behavior, failing gates (red CI), scope violations, security issues, data loss. - ⚠️ **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability debt worth fixing, but the PR works as shipped. - 💡 **SUGGESTION** — style, wording, import order, dartdoc refs, polish. Then map to the verdict: | Findings | `recommendation` | |---|---| | Any 🚨 BLOCKING (correctness/bug) | `REQUEST_CHANGES` — or `BLOCK` for security / data loss | | No 🚨 BLOCKING — only ⚠️ / 💡 remain | `APPROVE` | `APPROVE` with remaining ⚠️/💡 findings is the expected terminal state (`allowApproveWithSuggestions: true`): post every remaining finding as before (inline threads + general comment) — they do **not** block the merge and must **not** trigger another rework round. ## Anti-patterns (observed live, gh-71) - ❌ Returning `REQUEST_CHANGES` because a re-review surfaced new suggestion-level nits (docs wording, import style, dartdoc refs). A cycle with only suggestion-level findings **must** converge to `APPROVE`. - ❌ `REQUEST_CHANGES` while `issueCounts.blocking` is `0` — the machine treats that as an approval and skips the rework round. Keep `issueCounts` accurate: it is the machine's source of truth, not prose. The machine also cross-checks the counter against your inline comments (a `severity: "BLOCKING"` entry or a 🚨 marker in the referenced comment file) before honoring a blocking-0 approval — if any finding is truly blocking, set `recommendation: REQUEST_CHANGES` with `blocking: 1`+. - ❌ Verdict-by-prose: never phrase the verdict only in the summary text. The `recommendation` field of `outputs/pr_review.json` is the verdict. - ❌ 🚨 BLOCKING driven by an uncited external-spec claim ("the spec says X" without a `file:line` / doc URL the leg actually read). Downgrade it to a ⚠️ question; the machine treats BLOCKING threads as ground truth and arms rework on them. (Note: the post-action also downgrades such findings mechanically — keep the JSON consistent with the demoted severity so the census cross-check stays clean.) - ❌ Re-opening a thread that the rework demonstrably fixed in this diff — add its id to `resolvedThreadIds` instead. ## Label guard rails — the chore:pin lane (live: fa pr-1104, 2026-09-30) `chore:pin` is a trusted, **non-exclusive** factory fast-lane: several PRs may carry it at the same time (a release bump `chore/release-vX.Y.Z` AND a factory pin `chore/factory-pin-*` are both legitimate holders — they ride the lane independently). Reviews must therefore: - ❌ **NEVER remove `chore:pin` from any PR** — not as a "one pin" dedup, not as a side-effect of closing a related PR as superseded. Removing it from the release bump stranded the v1.0.494 tag behind the guest queue for an hour (fa pr-1104, unlabeled 13:31:08Z while pr-1105 was closed). - ✅ When a PR is superseded (e.g. a workflow change already shipped via another PR), close **only that PR** and leave every label on every other PR untouched. Label restoration is a keeper action, not yours. - ✅ If you believe two `chore:pin` holders conflict, SAY SO in the review comment and keep both labels — the owner resolves the lane, the machine only merges.

Goal — Extended Factory State Retention & Card Lifecycle History Preservation (v1)

**The factory state publisher (`js/factoryState.js`) retains merged PR cards for 7 days (up from 24 hours), keeps up to 500 snapshot entries in `<base>-history.json` (up from 72), and preserves up to 100 per-card state transitions in `card.history` (up from 24), so the factory board (`dmtools-factory`) can render multi-day timelines, time-travel across days, and retain full card lifecycle histories without premature truncation.**

Today, `js/factoryState.js` enforces three aggressive retention caps designed only for a short 6-hour / 24-hour window:
1. `MERGED_WINDOW_MS = 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000` (24 hours): merged PRs drop out of `lanes.merged_recent` 24 hours after `merged_at`. Worse, because `prevIndex(prev)` carries forward accumulated lifecycle timestamps (`reviewedAt`, `approvedAt`, `validatingAt`) and `card.history` only for cards still present in `prev`, once a merged PR leaves `merged_recent` its accumulated lifecycle metadata is permanently lost from the rolling state.
2. `HISTORY_KEEP = 72`: `updateHistory()` writes every timestamped snapshot file `data/<base>-<stamp>.json` to the `factory-data` branch (never deleting the files), but slices the `snapshots` index in `data/<base>-history.json` to `72` entries (~6 hours at 5-minute ticks), making older snapshots unreachable from the board's time-travel slider.
3. `HISTORY_CAP = 24`: `capHistory()` slices `card.history` (`[{ state, at }, ...]`) to the last 24 transitions, truncating the earliest transitions on long-lived or multi-rework cards.

## Architecture & Constants (`js/factoryState.js`)

| Constant | Current Value | New Value | Rationale |
|----------|---------------|-----------|-----------|
| `MERGED_WINDOW_MS` | `24 * 60 * 60 * 1000` (24h) | `7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000` (7 days) | Keeps merged PR cards and their accumulated lifecycle timestamps/history in `lanes.merged_recent` for a full week |
| `HISTORY_KEEP` | `72` (~6h of 5m ticks) | `500` (~41h+ of 5m ticks) | Expands `data/<base>-history.json` index so the board time-travel slider covers multi-day history while keeping JSON payload size small (~80 KB) |
| `HISTORY_CAP` | `24` transitions | `100` transitions | Preserves full card state transition history from `issue_created` / `pr_created` through `merged` even across multiple review/rework/validation cycles |

### Invariants
- `cfg.historyKeep` override in `updateHistory(state, cfg, exec)` continues to take precedence when explicitly passed by callers/tests (`var keep = (cfg && cfg.historyKeep) || HISTORY_KEEP;`).
- `SCHEMA_VERSION` stays `2` (additive retention widening; no schema shape break).
- Existing behavior for cards outside the widened 7-day `MERGED_WINDOW_MS` remains identical (dropped cleanly with no orphan token rows).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1 — 7-day merged PR retention (`MERGED_WINDOW_MS`):** `MERGED_WINDOW_MS` is `7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000` (`604800000`). A merged PR whose `merged_at` is within 7 days of `now` (e.g. 2 days or 6 days ago) stays in `lanes.merged_recent` and preserves its `prev` lifecycle timestamps (`reviewedAt`, `approvedAt`, `validatingAt`), `card.history`, and `card.tokens`; a merged PR older than 7 days is excluded.
- **AC2 — 500-snapshot history index (`HISTORY_KEEP`):** `HISTORY_KEEP` is `500` (and exported on `module.exports` if needed for test assertions). `updateHistory()` defaults to keeping up to `500` snapshots in `<base>-history.json` when `cfg.historyKeep` is not specified, while still honoring an explicit `cfg.historyKeep` override.
- **AC3 — 100-transition card history cap (`HISTORY_CAP`):** `HISTORY_CAP` is `100`. `capHistory()` retains up to `100` `{ state, at }` transitions per card before slicing to the most recent `100`.
- **AC4 — Unit test suite updated and green:** `js/unit-tests/test_factoryState.js` (and any sibling unit tests touching `merged_recent` window or `HISTORY_CAP` / `HISTORY_KEEP`) is updated for the new bounds and passes 100%.

## Test plan

- `UT-1` (**AC1**): Verify `buildFactoryState` retains merged PRs at 48h and 6d23h inside `lanes.merged_recent` (including carry-over from `prev` and token attachment), and drops merged PRs at >7d (e.g. 8 days before `now`).
- `UT-2` (**AC2**): Verify `updateHistory` default cap retains >72 snapshots (up to 500) and slices at 500 when `cfg.historyKeep` is omitted, and still trims to `cfg.historyKeep` when explicitly provided.
- `UT-3` (**AC3**): Verify `capHistory` / `nextHistory` keeps 50 transitions intact and caps at 100 when >100 transitions are accumulated.
- `REG-1` (**AC4**): `node js/unit-tests/test_factoryState.js` passes with zero failures.

## Non-goals
- Changing token ledger window (`DEFAULT_WINDOW_DAYS = 14` / `ROW_KEEP = 40` in `js/factory/token_usage.js` and `scripts/publish-token-usage.sh`) — out of scope for this issue.
- Deleting historical `data/<base>-<stamp>.json` files from the `factory-data` branch.

Goal — Extended Factory State Retention & Card Lifecycle History Preservation (v1)

**The factory state publisher (`js/factoryState.js`) retains merged PR cards for 7 days (up from 24 hours), keeps up to 500 snapshot entries in `<base>-history.json` (up from 72), and preserves up to 100 per-card state transitions in `card.history` (up from 24), so the factory board (`dmtools-factory`) can render multi-day timelines, time-travel across days, and retain full card lifecycle histories without premature truncation.**

Today, `js/factoryState.js` enforces three aggressive retention caps designed only for a short 6-hour / 24-hour window:
1. `MERGED_WINDOW_MS = 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000` (24 hours): merged PRs drop out of `lanes.merged_recent` 24 hours after `merged_at`. Worse, because `prevIndex(prev)` carries forward accumulated lifecycle timestamps (`reviewedAt`, `approvedAt`, `validatingAt`) and `card.history` only for cards still present in `prev`, once a merged PR leaves `merged_recent` its accumulated lifecycle metadata is permanently lost from the rolling state.
2. `HISTORY_KEEP = 72`: `updateHistory()` writes every timestamped snapshot file `data/<base>-<stamp>.json` to the `factory-data` branch (never deleting the files), but slices the `snapshots` index in `data/<base>-history.json` to `72` entries (~6 hours at 5-minute ticks), making older snapshots unreachable from the board's time-travel slider.
3. `HISTORY_CAP = 24`: `capHistory()` slices `card.history` (`[{ state, at }, ...]`) to the last 24 transitions, truncating the earliest transitions on long-lived or multi-rework cards.

## Architecture & Constants (`js/factoryState.js`)

| Constant | Current Value | New Value | Rationale |
|----------|---------------|-----------|-----------|
| `MERGED_WINDOW_MS` | `24 * 60 * 60 * 1000` (24h) | `7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000` (7 days) | Keeps merged PR cards and their accumulated lifecycle timestamps/history in `lanes.merged_recent` for a full week |
| `HISTORY_KEEP` | `72` (~6h of 5m ticks) | `500` (~41h+ of 5m ticks) | Expands `data/<base>-history.json` index so the board time-travel slider covers multi-day history while keeping JSON payload size small (~80 KB) |
| `HISTORY_CAP` | `24` transitions | `100` transitions | Preserves full card state transition history from `issue_created` / `pr_created` through `merged` even across multiple review/rework/validation cycles |

### Invariants
- `cfg.historyKeep` override in `updateHistory(state, cfg, exec)` continues to take precedence when explicitly passed by callers/tests (`var keep = (cfg && cfg.historyKeep) || HISTORY_KEEP;`).
- `SCHEMA_VERSION` stays `2` (additive retention widening; no schema shape break).
- Existing behavior for cards outside the widened 7-day `MERGED_WINDOW_MS` remains identical (dropped cleanly with no orphan token rows).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1 — 7-day merged PR retention (`MERGED_WINDOW_MS`):** `MERGED_WINDOW_MS` is `7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000` (`604800000`). A merged PR whose `merged_at` is within 7 days of `now` (e.g. 2 days or 6 days ago) stays in `lanes.merged_recent` and preserves its `prev` lifecycle timestamps (`reviewedAt`, `approvedAt`, `validatingAt`), `card.history`, and `card.tokens`; a merged PR older than 7 days is excluded.
- **AC2 — 500-snapshot history index (`HISTORY_KEEP`):** `HISTORY_KEEP` is `500` (and exported on `module.exports` if needed for test assertions). `updateHistory()` defaults to keeping up to `500` snapshots in `<base>-history.json` when `cfg.historyKeep` is not specified, while still honoring an explicit `cfg.historyKeep` override.
- **AC3 — 100-transition card history cap (`HISTORY_CAP`):** `HISTORY_CAP` is `100`. `capHistory()` retains up to `100` `{ state, at }` transitions per card before slicing to the most recent `100`.
- **AC4 — Unit test suite updated and green:** `js/unit-tests/test_factoryState.js` (and any sibling unit tests touching `merged_recent` window or `HISTORY_CAP` / `HISTORY_KEEP`) is updated for the new bounds and passes 100%.

## Test plan

- `UT-1` (**AC1**): Verify `buildFactoryState` retains merged PRs at 48h and 6d23h inside `lanes.merged_recent` (including carry-over from `prev` and token attachment), and drops merged PRs at >7d (e.g. 8 days before `now`).
- `UT-2` (**AC2**): Verify `updateHistory` default cap retains >72 snapshots (up to 500) and slices at 500 when `cfg.historyKeep` is omitted, and still trims to `cfg.historyKeep` when explicitly provided.
- `UT-3` (**AC3**): Verify `capHistory` / `nextHistory` keeps 50 transitions intact and caps at 100 when >100 transitions are accumulated.
- `REG-1` (**AC4**): `node js/unit-tests/test_factoryState.js` passes with zero failures.

## Non-goals
- Changing token ledger window (`DEFAULT_WINDOW_DAYS = 14` / `ROW_KEEP = 40` in `js/factory/token_usage.js` and `scripts/publish-token-usage.sh`) — out of scope for this issue.
- Deleting historical `data/<base>-<stamp>.json` files from the `factory-data` branch.

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-21):
🚨 **BLOCKING: the 7d window × the 100-PR merged feed pushes the state snapshot past the executor's command-size ceiling — `publishFactoryState` fails on every tick, board silently goes stale**

`github_list_prs state:'merged'` (the `mergedPrs` producer, `js/common/smProvider.js:265-273`) returns a page of **100 merged PRs**. For this repo right now that page spans only **4.4 days** of merges (~23/day): 4 of those PRs fall inside the current 24h window, but **all 100 fall inside the new 7d window**. `merged_recent` therefore grows from ~4-8 cards to 100 cards on every tick.

I built the state with the live 100-PR feed through the real `buildFactoryState` (real titles/refs, realistic carried stamps, 6-entry histories, `checks`, `tokens` rows — the fields `mergedPrCard`/`carryTimestamps`/`mergedChecksFor` produce):

```
24h window (today):  8 cards  → state JSON     4,818B
7d window (this PR): 100 cards → state JSON 104,489B  ❌
```

**104,489B is past the hard transport ceiling.** `snapshotPutCommand` emits
`gh api -X PUT … -f content="$(printf %s '<json>' | base64)"`. I probed this
exact command shape on the installed dmtools binary (`cli_execute_command`):
the base64-expanded content becomes a single `execve` argument, and Linux
`MAX_ARG_STRLEN` (131,072B) kills it — bisected break point at **~96.7KB of
JSON payload** (96,752B passes, 97,632B fails with exit 126 `Argument list
too long`). Today's state (~5-20KB) is far under it; this PR crosses it
deterministically at the current merge rate.

Failure mode is silent: `js/smAgent.js:5537-5541` catches the throw and only
logs `⚠️ factory state publish failed` — the tick stays green while the board
stops updating (state, mutex, rework-latch, alarms persistence all ride this
snapshot).

Suggested directions (any one):
- Cap the lane like `BACKLOG_CAP` (`js/factoryState.js:1006-1008` precedent): keep the 7d semantics, `.slice(0, MERGED_LANE_CAP)` the newest ~40-50 cards.
- Thin merged-card payloads (drop `checks`/`tokens`/history bulk for terminal cards).
- Fix the transport (temp file + `gh api --input`), which lifts the ceiling for both this and the history index.

Either way, please add a REG guard asserting the built state JSON stays under the measured ceiling, so this can't regress silently.

Here the JSON is embedded via shellQuote — it becomes part of ONE argument? No wait — the command string is `sh -c`'d (the whole script is interpreted by sh line by line). Within the script, the line is: `gh api ... -f content="$(printf %s '....127KB....' | base64)"`. When sh parses this line, the argument to `printf` is the 127KB single-quoted string → printf's argv contains a ~127KB argument → execve(printf)... printf is usually a shell BUILTIN in dash/sh — builtins don't execve, so no MAX_ARG_STRLEN applies to builtins!

Goal — Extended Factory State Retention & Card Lifecycle History Preservation (v1)

**The factory state publisher (`js/factoryState.js`) retains merged PR cards for 7 days (up from 24 hours), keeps up to 500 snapshot entries in `<base>-history.json` (up from 72), and preserves up to 100 per-card state transitions in `card.history` (up from 24), so the factory board (`dmtools-factory`) can render multi-day timelines, time-travel across days, and retain full card lifecycle histories without premature truncation.**

Today, `js/factoryState.js` enforces three aggressive retention caps designed only for a short 6-hour / 24-hour window:
1. `MERGED_WINDOW_MS = 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000` (24 hours): merged PRs drop out of `lanes.merged_recent` 24 hours after `merged_at`. Worse, because `prevIndex(prev)` carries forward accumulated lifecycle timestamps (`reviewedAt`, `approvedAt`, `validatingAt`) and `card.history` only for cards still present in `prev`, once a merged PR leaves `merged_recent` its accumulated lifecycle metadata is permanently lost from the rolling state.
2. `HISTORY_KEEP = 72`: `updateHistory()` writes every timestamped snapshot file `data/<base>-<stamp>.json` to the `factory-data` branch (never deleting the files), but slices the `snapshots` index in `data/<base>-history.json` to `72` entries (~6 hours at 5-minute ticks), making older snapshots unreachable from the board's time-travel slider.
3. `HISTORY_CAP = 24`: `capHistory()` slices `card.history` (`[{ state, at }, ...]`) to the last 24 transitions, truncating the earliest transitions on long-lived or multi-rework cards.

## Architecture & Constants (`js/factoryState.js`)

| Constant | Current Value | New Value | Rationale |
|----------|---------------|-----------|-----------|
| `MERGED_WINDOW_MS` | `24 * 60 * 60 * 1000` (24h) | `7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000` (7 days) | Keeps merged PR cards and their accumulated lifecycle timestamps/history in `lanes.merged_recent` for a full week |
| `HISTORY_KEEP` | `72` (~6h of 5m ticks) | `500` (~41h+ of 5m ticks) | Expands `data/<base>-history.json` index so the board time-travel slider covers multi-day history while keeping JSON payload size small (~80 KB) |
| `HISTORY_CAP` | `24` transitions | `100` transitions | Preserves full card state transition history from `issue_created` / `pr_created` through `merged` even across multiple review/rework/validation cycles |

### Invariants
- `cfg.historyKeep` override in `updateHistory(state, cfg, exec)` continues to take precedence when explicitly passed by callers/tests (`var keep = (cfg && cfg.historyKeep) || HISTORY_KEEP;`).
- `SCHEMA_VERSION` stays `2` (additive retention widening; no schema shape break).
- Existing behavior for cards outside the widened 7-day `MERGED_WINDOW_MS` remains identical (dropped cleanly with no orphan token rows).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1 — 7-day merged PR retention (`MERGED_WINDOW_MS`):** `MERGED_WINDOW_MS` is `7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000` (`604800000`). A merged PR whose `merged_at` is within 7 days of `now` (e.g. 2 days or 6 days ago) stays in `lanes.merged_recent` and preserves its `prev` lifecycle timestamps (`reviewedAt`, `approvedAt`, `validatingAt`), `card.history`, and `card.tokens`; a merged PR older than 7 days is excluded.
- **AC2 — 500-snapshot history index (`HISTORY_KEEP`):** `HISTORY_KEEP` is `500` (and exported on `module.exports` if needed for test assertions). `updateHistory()` defaults to keeping up to `500` snapshots in `<base>-history.json` when `cfg.historyKeep` is not specified, while still honoring an explicit `cfg.historyKeep` override.
- **AC3 — 100-transition card history cap (`HISTORY_CAP`):** `HISTORY_CAP` is `100`. `capHistory()` retains up to `100` `{ state, at }` transitions per card before slicing to the most recent `100`.
- **AC4 — Unit test suite updated and green:** `js/unit-tests/test_factoryState.js` (and any sibling unit tests touching `merged_recent` window or `HISTORY_CAP` / `HISTORY_KEEP`) is updated for the new bounds and passes 100%.

## Test plan

- `UT-1` (**AC1**): Verify `buildFactoryState` retains merged PRs at 48h and 6d23h inside `lanes.merged_recent` (including carry-over from `prev` and token attachment), and drops merged PRs at >7d (e.g. 8 days before `now`).
- `UT-2` (**AC2**): Verify `updateHistory` default cap retains >72 snapshots (up to 500) and slices at 500 when `cfg.historyKeep` is omitted, and still trims to `cfg.historyKeep` when explicitly provided.
- `UT-3` (**AC3**): Verify `capHistory` / `nextHistory` keeps 50 transitions intact and caps at 100 when >100 transitions are accumulated.
- `REG-1` (**AC4**): `node js/unit-tests/test_factoryState.js` passes with zero failures.

## Non-goals
- Changing token ledger window (`DEFAULT_WINDOW_DAYS = 14` / `ROW_KEEP = 40` in `js/factory/token_usage.js` and `scripts/publish-token-usage.sh`) — out of scope for this issue.
- Deleting historical `data/<base>-<stamp>.json` files from the `factory-data` branch.

Goal — Extended Factory State Retention & Card Lifecycle History Preservation (v1)

**The factory state publisher (`js/factoryState.js`) retains merged PR cards for 7 days (up from 24 hours), keeps up to 500 snapshot entries in `<base>-history.json` (up from 72), and preserves up to 100 per-card state transitions in `card.history` (up from 24), so the factory board (`dmtools-factory`) can render multi-day timelines, time-travel across days, and retain full card lifecycle histories without premature truncation.**

Today, `js/factoryState.js` enforces three aggressive retention caps designed only for a short 6-hour / 24-hour window:
1. `MERGED_WINDOW_MS = 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000` (24 hours): merged PRs drop out of `lanes.merged_recent` 24 hours after `merged_at`. Worse, because `prevIndex(prev)` carries forward accumulated lifecycle timestamps (`reviewedAt`, `approvedAt`, `validatingAt`) and `card.history` only for cards still present in `prev`, once a merged PR leaves `merged_recent` its accumulated lifecycle metadata is permanently lost from the rolling state.
2. `HISTORY_KEEP = 72`: `updateHistory()` writes every timestamped snapshot file `data/<base>-<stamp>.json` to the `factory-data` branch (never deleting the files), but slices the `snapshots` index in `data/<base>-history.json` to `72` entries (~6 hours at 5-minute ticks), making older snapshots unreachable from the board's time-travel slider.
3. `HISTORY_CAP = 24`: `capHistory()` slices `card.history` (`[{ state, at }, ...]`) to the last 24 transitions, truncating the earliest transitions on long-lived or multi-rework cards.

## Architecture & Constants (`js/factoryState.js`)

| Constant | Current Value | New Value | Rationale |
|----------|---------------|-----------|-----------|
| `MERGED_WINDOW_MS` | `24 * 60 * 60 * 1000` (24h) | `7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000` (7 days) | Keeps merged PR cards and their accumulated lifecycle timestamps/history in `lanes.merged_recent` for a full week |
| `HISTORY_KEEP` | `72` (~6h of 5m ticks) | `500` (~41h+ of 5m ticks) | Expands `data/<base>-history.json` index so the board time-travel slider covers multi-day history while keeping JSON payload size small (~80 KB) |
| `HISTORY_CAP` | `24` transitions | `100` transitions | Preserves full card state transition history from `issue_created` / `pr_created` through `merged` even across multiple review/rework/validation cycles |

### Invariants
- `cfg.historyKeep` override in `updateHistory(state, cfg, exec)` continues to take precedence when explicitly passed by callers/tests (`var keep = (cfg && cfg.historyKeep) || HISTORY_KEEP;`).
- `SCHEMA_VERSION` stays `2` (additive retention widening; no schema shape break).
- Existing behavior for cards outside the widened 7-day `MERGED_WINDOW_MS` remains identical (dropped cleanly with no orphan token rows).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1 — 7-day merged PR retention (`MERGED_WINDOW_MS`):** `MERGED_WINDOW_MS` is `7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000` (`604800000`). A merged PR whose `merged_at` is within 7 days of `now` (e.g. 2 days or 6 days ago) stays in `lanes.merged_recent` and preserves its `prev` lifecycle timestamps (`reviewedAt`, `approvedAt`, `validatingAt`), `card.history`, and `card.tokens`; a merged PR older than 7 days is excluded.
- **AC2 — 500-snapshot history index (`HISTORY_KEEP`):** `HISTORY_KEEP` is `500` (and exported on `module.exports` if needed for test assertions). `updateHistory()` defaults to keeping up to `500` snapshots in `<base>-history.json` when `cfg.historyKeep` is not specified, while still honoring an explicit `cfg.historyKeep` override.
- **AC3 — 100-transition card history cap (`HISTORY_CAP`):** `HISTORY_CAP` is `100`. `capHistory()` retains up to `100` `{ state, at }` transitions per card before slicing to the most recent `100`.
- **AC4 — Unit test suite updated and green:** `js/unit-tests/test_factoryState.js` (and any sibling unit tests touching `merged_recent` window or `HISTORY_CAP` / `HISTORY_KEEP`) is updated for the new bounds and passes 100%.

## Test plan

- `UT-1` (**AC1**): Verify `buildFactoryState` retains merged PRs at 48h and 6d23h inside `lanes.merged_recent` (including carry-over from `prev` and token attachment), and drops merged PRs at >7d (e.g. 8 days before `now`).
- `UT-2` (**AC2**): Verify `updateHistory` default cap retains >72 snapshots (up to 500) and slices at 500 when `cfg.historyKeep` is omitted, and still trims to `cfg.historyKeep` when explicitly provided.
- `UT-3` (**AC3**): Verify `capHistory` / `nextHistory` keeps 50 transitions intact and caps at 100 when >100 transitions are accumulated.
- `REG-1` (**AC4**): `node js/unit-tests/test_factoryState.js` passes with zero failures.

## Non-goals
- Changing token ledger window (`DEFAULT_WINDOW_DAYS = 14` / `ROW_KEEP = 40` in `js/factory/token_usage.js` and `scripts/publish-token-usage.sh`) — out of scope for this issue.
- Deleting historical `data/<base>-<stamp>.json` files from the `factory-data` branch.

Goal — Extended Factory State Retention & Card Lifecycle History Preservation (v1)

**The factory state publisher (`js/factoryState.js`) retains merged PR cards for 7 days (up from 24 hours), keeps up to 500 snapshot entries in `<base>-history.json` (up from 72), and preserves up to 100 per-card state transitions in `card.history` (up from 24), so the factory board (`dmtools-factory`) can render multi-day timelines, time-travel across days, and retain full card lifecycle histories without premature truncation.**

Today, `js/factoryState.js` enforces three aggressive retention caps designed only for a short 6-hour / 24-hour window:
1. `MERGED_WINDOW_MS = 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000` (24 hours): merged PRs drop out of `lanes.merged_recent` 24 hours after `merged_at`. Worse, because `prevIndex(prev)` carries forward accumulated lifecycle timestamps (`reviewedAt`, `approvedAt`, `validatingAt`) and `card.history` only for cards still present in `prev`, once a merged PR leaves `merged_recent` its accumulated lifecycle metadata is permanently lost from the rolling state.
2. `HISTORY_KEEP = 72`: `updateHistory()` writes every timestamped snapshot file `data/<base>-<stamp>.json` to the `factory-data` branch (never deleting the files), but slices the `snapshots` index in `data/<base>-history.json` to `72` entries (~6 hours at 5-minute ticks), making older snapshots unreachable from the board's time-travel slider.
3. `HISTORY_CAP = 24`: `capHistory()` slices `card.history` (`[{ state, at }, ...]`) to the last 24 transitions, truncating the earliest transitions on long-lived or multi-rework cards.

## Architecture & Constants (`js/factoryState.js`)

| Constant | Current Value | New Value | Rationale |
|----------|---------------|-----------|-----------|
| `MERGED_WINDOW_MS` | `24 * 60 * 60 * 1000` (24h) | `7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000` (7 days) | Keeps merged PR cards and their accumulated lifecycle timestamps/history in `lanes.merged_recent` for a full week |
| `HISTORY_KEEP` | `72` (~6h of 5m ticks) | `500` (~41h+ of 5m ticks) | Expands `data/<base>-history.json` index so the board time-travel slider covers multi-day history while keeping JSON payload size small (~80 KB) |
| `HISTORY_CAP` | `24` transitions | `100` transitions | Preserves full card state transition history from `issue_created` / `pr_created` through `merged` even across multiple review/rework/validation cycles |

### Invariants
- `cfg.historyKeep` override in `updateHistory(state, cfg, exec)` continues to take precedence when explicitly passed by callers/tests (`var keep = (cfg && cfg.historyKeep) || HISTORY_KEEP;`).
- `SCHEMA_VERSION` stays `2` (additive retention widening; no schema shape break).
- Existing behavior for cards outside the widened 7-day `MERGED_WINDOW_MS` remains identical (dropped cleanly with no orphan token rows).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1 — 7-day merged PR retention (`MERGED_WINDOW_MS`):** `MERGED_WINDOW_MS` is `7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000` (`604800000`). A merged PR whose `merged_at` is within 7 days of `now` (e.g. 2 days or 6 days ago) stays in `lanes.merged_recent` and preserves its `prev` lifecycle timestamps (`reviewedAt`, `approvedAt`, `validatingAt`), `card.history`, and `card.tokens`; a merged PR older than 7 days is excluded.
- **AC2 — 500-snapshot history index (`HISTORY_KEEP`):** `HISTORY_KEEP` is `500` (and exported on `module.exports` if needed for test assertions). `updateHistory()` defaults to keeping up to `500` snapshots in `<base>-history.json` when `cfg.historyKeep` is not specified, while still honoring an explicit `cfg.historyKeep` override.
- **AC3 — 100-transition card history cap (`HISTORY_CAP`):** `HISTORY_CAP` is `100`. `capHistory()` retains up to `100` `{ state, at }` transitions per card before slicing to the most recent `100`.
- **AC4 — Unit test suite updated and green:** `js/unit-tests/test_factoryState.js` (and any sibling unit tests touching `merged_recent` window or `HISTORY_CAP` / `HISTORY_KEEP`) is updated for the new bounds and passes 100%.

## Test plan

- `UT-1` (**AC1**): Verify `buildFactoryState` retains merged PRs at 48h and 6d23h inside `lanes.merged_recent` (including carry-over from `prev` and token attachment), and drops merged PRs at >7d (e.g. 8 days before `now`).
- `UT-2` (**AC2**): Verify `updateHistory` default cap retains >72 snapshots (up to 500) and slices at 500 when `cfg.historyKeep` is omitted, and still trims to `cfg.historyKeep` when explicitly provided.
- `UT-3` (**AC3**): Verify `capHistory` / `nextHistory` keeps 50 transitions intact and caps at 100 when >100 transitions are accumulated.
- `REG-1` (**AC4**): `node js/unit-tests/test_factoryState.js` passes with zero failures.

## Non-goals
- Changing token ledger window (`DEFAULT_WINDOW_DAYS = 14` / `ROW_KEEP = 40` in `js/factory/token_usage.js` and `scripts/publish-token-usage.sh`) — out of scope for this issue.
- Deleting historical `data/<base>-<stamp>.json` files from the `factory-data` branch.

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1151._

> ℹ️ **1 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `js/factoryState.js` line 185

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-21):
🚨 **BLOCKING: the 7d window × the 100-PR merged feed pushes the state snapshot past the executor's command-size ceiling — `publishFactoryState` fails on every tick, board silently goes stale**

`github_list_prs state:'merged'` (the `mergedPrs` producer, `js/common/smProvider.js:265-273`) returns a page of **100 merged PRs**. For this repo right now that page spans only **4.4 days** of merges (~23/day): 4 of those PRs fall inside the current 24h window, but **all 100 fall inside the new 7d window**. `merged_recent` therefore grows from ~4-8 cards to 100 cards on every tick.

I built the state with the live 100-PR feed through the real `buildFactoryState` (real titles/refs, realistic carried stamps, 6-entry histories, `checks`, `tokens` rows — the fields `mergedPrCard`/`carryTimestamps`/`mergedChecksFor` produce):

```
24h window (today):  8 cards  → state JSON     4,818B
7d window (this PR): 100 cards → state JSON 104,489B  ❌
```

**104,489B is past the hard transport ceiling.** `snapshotPutCommand` emits
`gh api -X PUT … -f content="$(printf %s '<json>' | base64)"`. I probed this
exact command shape on the installed dmtools binary (`cli_execute_command`):
the base64-expanded content becomes a single `execve` argument, and Linux
`MAX_ARG_STRLEN` (131,072B) kills it — bisected break point at **~96.7KB of
JSON payload** (96,752B passes, 97,632B fails with exit 126 `Argument list
too long`). Today's state (~5-20KB) is far under it; this PR crosses it
deterministically at the current merge rate.

Failure mode is silent: `js/smAgent.js:5537-5541` catches the throw and only
logs `⚠️ factory state publish failed` — the tick stays green while the board
stops updating (state, mutex, rework-latch, alarms persistence all ride this
snapshot).

Suggested directions (any one):
- Cap the lane like `BACKLOG_CAP` (`js/factoryState.js:1006-1008` precedent): keep the 7d semantics, `.slice(0, MERGED_LANE_CAP)` the newest ~40-50 cards.
- Thin merged-card payloads (drop `checks`/`tokens`/history bulk for terminal cards).
- Fix the transport (temp file + `gh api --input`), which lifts the ceiling for both this and the history index.

Either way, please add a REG guard asserting the built state JSON stays under the measured ceiling, so this can't regress silently.

---

### Thread 2 — `js/factoryState.js` line 207

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-21):
🚨 **BLOCKING: HISTORY_KEEP=500 builds a history index that deterministically exceeds the executor's command-size ceiling — `updateHistory` fails permanently once the index fills**

`historyPutCommand` emits the same `-f content="$(printf %s '<json>' | base64)"`
shape as the state PUT, so the index JSON rides a single `execve` argument
capped by Linux `MAX_ARG_STRLEN` (131,072B). I probed this exact shape on the
installed dmtools binary: **~96.7KB of JSON is the ceiling** (96,752B OK,
97,632B → exit 126 `Argument list too long`).

The index size is deterministic — every entry's `ts`/`tick` are ISO stamps and
`url` is `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/<repo>/<branch>/data/<base>-<stamp>.json`
(~197B/entry). Rebuilt exactly as `updateHistory` writes it:

```
keep= 72 (today): 14,265B  ✅
keep=465:          91,685B  ✅ (last safe point)
keep=500 (this PR):98,580B  ❌ over the ceiling
```

The index grows monotonically after rollout (one entry per tick, trimmed to
`keep`), so ~1.7 days in (at the 5-min cadence this ticket assumes; ~3.5d at
10-min) the PUT starts failing **on every subsequent tick forever**: the retry
re-reads the stuck index, unshifts one entry, trims to 500 — always over the
ceiling. `js/smAgent.js:5543-5549` swallows it as
`⚠️ factory state history failed`, so the board's time-travel slider silently
freezes just short of the depth this ticket bought.

Note the ticket itself justifies 500 with *"keeping JSON payload size small
(~80 KB)"* — that assumption is empirically false: with real URL/stamp shapes
the 500-entry index is 98.6KB, past the measured break.

Fix: bound the default to ≤ ~450 (ceiling ÷ ~197B/entry, with headroom) and
add a REG test asserting the built index stays under the ceiling — or fix the
transport (temp file + `gh api --input`), which lifts the ceiling for the
state snapshot too.

---

### Thread 3 — `js/factoryState.js` line 260

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-21):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the "~4h" eviction math in this comment is now stale — it was computed for the old `HISTORY_CAP = 24`**

The guard this comment documents is unchanged, but the number below it no
longer follows from the constants this PR edits: without the dedupe guard,
each tick appends a duplicate terminal entry and the cap starts evicting the
real timeline after `HISTORY_CAP` ticks. At the new `HISTORY_CAP = 100` that
is **~16.7h at the 10-min cadence** (~8.3h at 5-min), not "~4h" (which is
24 × 10min, the old cap).

One-line comment fix so the motivation quoted in `test_factoryState.js:563-565`
and the code stay in sync.

---

### Thread 4 — `js/unit-tests/test_factoryState.js` line 1133

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-21):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the AC2 test re-implements the exec-mock scaffolding of the neighboring index test — extract a small helper**

`gh-1150 AC2` (this test) and `updateHistory: existing index — append, carry
sha, trim to keep` (js/unit-tests/test_factoryState.js:1101-1130) duplicate the
same ~15-line mock: probe `--jq .sha` → `'feedface'`, probe `--jq .content` →
`JSON.stringify(old)`, then fish the last PUT out of `seen` and regex-extract
`"url":"…"` pairs. A tiny helper, e.g.

```js
function withHistoryIndex(snaps, run) {
  var seen = [];
  fsModule.updateHistory(ST,
    { repo: 'IstiN/flutter_agent_harness', asset: 'fa-state.json', historyKeep: snaps.keep },
    function (a) {
      seen.push(a.command);
      if (a.command.indexOf('--jq .sha') > 0) return { output: 'feedface\n' };

## Summary

Implements **gh-1150** — extends factory state retention and card lifecycle history caps in `js/factoryState.js`:

Goal — Extended Factory State Retention & Card Lifecycle History Preservation (v1)

**The factory state publisher (`js/factoryState.js`) retains merged PR cards for 7 days (up from 24 hours), keeps up to 500 snapshot entries in `<base>-history.json` (up from 72), and preserves up to 100 per-card state transitions in `card.history` (up from 24), so the factory board (`dmtools-factory`) can render multi-day timelines, time-travel across days, and retain full card lifecycle histories without premature truncation.**

Today, `js/factoryState.js` enforces three aggressive retention caps designed only for a short 6-hour / 24-hour window:
1. `MERGED_WINDOW_MS = 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000` (24 hours): merged PRs drop out of `lanes.merged_recent` 24 hours after `merged_at`. Worse, because `prevIndex(prev)` carries forward accumulated lifecycle timestamps (`reviewedAt`, `approvedAt`, `validatingAt`) and `card.history` only for cards still present in `prev`, once a merged PR leaves `merged_recent` its accumulated lifecycle metadata is permanently lost from the rolling state.
2. `HISTORY_KEEP = 72`: `updateHistory()` writes every timestamped snapshot file `data/<base>-<stamp>.json` to the `factory-data` branch (never deleting the files), but slices the `snapshots` index in `data/<base>-history.json` to `72` entries (~6 hours at 5-minute ticks), making older snapshots unreachable from the board's time-travel slider.
3. `HISTORY_CAP = 24`: `capHistory()` slices `card.history` (`[{ state, at }, ...]`) to the last 24 transitions, truncating the earliest transitions on long-lived or multi-rework cards.

## Architecture & Constants (`js/factoryState.js`)

| Constant | Current Value | New Value | Rationale |
|----------|---------------|-----------|-----------|
| `MERGED_WINDOW_MS` | `24 * 60 * 60 * 1000` (24h) | `7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000` (7 days) | Keeps merged PR cards and their accumulated lifecycle timestamps/history in `lanes.merged_recent` for a full week |
| `HISTORY_KEEP` | `72` (~6h of 5m ticks) | `500` (~41h+ of 5m ticks) | Expands `data/<base>-history.json` index so the board time-travel slider covers multi-day history while keeping JSON payload size small (~80 KB) |
| `HISTORY_CAP` | `24` transitions | `100` transitions | Preserves full card state transition history from `issue_created` / `pr_created` through `merged` even across multiple review/rework/validation cycles |

### Invariants
- `cfg.historyKeep` override in `updateHistory(state, cfg, exec)` continues to take precedence when explicitly passed by callers/tests (`var keep = (cfg && cfg.historyKeep) || HISTORY_KEEP;`).
- `SCHEMA_VERSION` stays `2` (additive retention widening; no schema shape break).
- Existing behavior for cards outside the widened 7-day `MERGED_WINDOW_MS` remains identical (dropped cleanly with no orphan token rows).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1 — 7-day merged PR retention (`MERGED_WINDOW_MS`):** `MERGED_WINDOW_MS` is `7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000` (`604800000`). A merged PR whose `merged_at` is within 7 days of `now` (e.g. 2 days or 6 days ago) stays in `lanes.merged_recent` and preserves its `prev` lifecycle timestamps (`reviewedAt`, `approvedAt`, `validatingAt`), `card.history`, and `card.tokens`; a merged PR older than 7 days is excluded.
- **AC2 — 500-snapshot history index (`HISTORY_KEEP`):** `HISTORY_KEEP` is `500` (and exported on `module.exports` if needed for test assertions). `updateHistory()` defaults to keeping up to `500` snapshots in `<base>-history.json` when `cfg.historyKeep` is not specified, while still honoring an explicit `cfg.historyKeep` override.
- **AC3 — 100-transition card history cap (`HISTORY_CAP`):** `HISTORY_CAP` is `100`. `capHistory()` retains up to `100` `{ state, at }` transitions per card before slicing to the most recent `100`.
- **AC4 — Unit test suite updated and green:** `js/unit-tests/test_factoryState.js` (and any sibling unit tests touching `merged_recent` window or `HISTORY_CAP` / `HISTORY_KEEP`) is updated for the new bounds and passes 100%.

## Test plan

- `UT-1` (**AC1**): Verify `buildFactoryState` retains merged PRs at 48h and 6d23h inside `lanes.merged_recent` (including carry-over from `prev` and token attachment), and drops merged PRs at >7d (e.g. 8 days before `now`).
- `UT-2` (**AC2**): Verify `updateHistory` default cap retains >72 snapshots (up to 500) and slices at 500 when `cfg.historyKeep` is omitted, and still trims to `cfg.historyKeep` when explicitly provided.
- `UT-3` (**AC3**): Verify `capHistory` / `nextHistory` keeps 50 transitions intact and caps at 100 when >100 transitions are accumulated.
- `REG-1` (**AC4**): `node js/unit-tests/test_factoryState.js` passes with zero failures.

## Non-goals
- Changing token ledger window (`DEFAULT_WINDOW_DAYS = 14` / `ROW_KEEP = 40` in `js/factory/token_usage.js` and `scripts/publish-token-usage.sh`) — out of scope for this issue.
- Deleting historical `data/<base>-<stamp>.json` files from the `factory-data` branch.

Implements **gh-1150** — extends factory state retention and card lifecycle history caps in `js/factoryState.js`:

- **`MERGED_WINDOW_MS`**: `7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000` (7 days, up from 24h) so merged PR cards and their accumulated lifecycle timestamps (`reviewedAt`, `approvedAt`, `validatingAt`), `card.history`, and `card.tokens` remain in `lanes.merged_recent` for a full week.

Goal — Extended Factory State Retention & Card Lifecycle History Preservation (v1)

**The factory state publisher (`js/factoryState.js`) retains merged PR cards for 7 days (up from 24 hours), keeps up to 500 snapshot entries in `<base>-history.json` (up from 72), and preserves up to 100 per-card state transitions in `card.history` (up from 24), so the factory board (`dmtools-factory`) can render multi-day timelines, time-travel across days, and retain full card lifecycle histories without premature truncation.**

Today, `js/factoryState.js` enforces three aggressive retention caps designed only for a short 6-hour / 24-hour window:
1. `MERGED_WINDOW_MS = 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000` (24 hours): merged PRs drop out of `lanes.merged_recent` 24 hours after `merged_at`. Worse, because `prevIndex(prev)` carries forward accumulated lifecycle timestamps (`reviewedAt`, `approvedAt`, `validatingAt`) and `card.history` only for cards still present in `prev`, once a merged PR leaves `merged_recent` its accumulated lifecycle metadata is permanently lost from the rolling state.
2. `HISTORY_KEEP = 72`: `updateHistory()` writes every timestamped snapshot file `data/<base>-<stamp>.json` to the `factory-data` branch (never deleting the files), but slices the `snapshots` index in `data/<base>-history.json` to `72` entries (~6 hours at 5-minute ticks), making older snapshots unreachable from the board's time-travel slider.
3. `HISTORY_CAP = 24`: `capHistory()` slices `card.history` (`[{ state, at }, ...]`) to the last 24 transitions, truncating the earliest transitions on long-lived or multi-rework cards.

## Architecture & Constants (`js/factoryState.js`)

| Constant | Current Value | New Value | Rationale |
|----------|---------------|-----------|-----------|
| `MERGED_WINDOW_MS` | `24 * 60 * 60 * 1000` (24h) | `7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000` (7 days) | Keeps merged PR cards and their accumulated lifecycle timestamps/history in `lanes.merged_recent` for a full week |
| `HISTORY_KEEP` | `72` (~6h of 5m ticks) | `500` (~41h+ of 5m ticks) | Expands `data/<base>-history.json` index so the board time-travel slider covers multi-day history while keeping JSON payload size small (~80 KB) |
| `HISTORY_CAP` | `24` transitions | `100` transitions | Preserves full card state transition history from `issue_created` / `pr_created` through `merged` even across multiple review/rework/validation cycles |

### Invariants
- `cfg.historyKeep` override in `updateHistory(state, cfg, exec)` continues to take precedence when explicitly passed by callers/tests (`var keep = (cfg && cfg.historyKeep) || HISTORY_KEEP;`).
- `SCHEMA_VERSION` stays `2` (additive retention widening; no schema shape break).
- Existing behavior for cards outside the widened 7-day `MERGED_WINDOW_MS` remains identical (dropped cleanly with no orphan token rows).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1 — 7-day merged PR retention (`MERGED_WINDOW_MS`):** `MERGED_WINDOW_MS` is `7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000` (`604800000`). A merged PR whose `merged_at` is within 7 days of `now` (e.g. 2 days or 6 days ago) stays in `lanes.merged_recent` and preserves its `prev` lifecycle timestamps (`reviewedAt`, `approvedAt`, `validatingAt`), `card.history`, and `card.tokens`; a merged PR older than 7 days is excluded.
- **AC2 — 500-snapshot history index (`HISTORY_KEEP`):** `HISTORY_KEEP` is `500` (and exported on `module.exports` if needed for test assertions). `updateHistory()` defaults to keeping up to `500` snapshots in `<base>-history.json` when `cfg.historyKeep` is not specified, while still honoring an explicit `cfg.historyKeep` override.
- **AC3 — 100-transition card history cap (`HISTORY_CAP`):** `HISTORY_CAP` is `100`. `capHistory()` retains up to `100` `{ state, at }` transitions per card before slicing to the most recent `100`.
- **AC4 — Unit test suite updated and green:** `js/unit-tests/test_factoryState.js` (and any sibling unit tests touching `merged_recent` window or `HISTORY_CAP` / `HISTORY_KEEP`) is updated for the new bounds and passes 100%.

## Test plan

- `UT-1` (**AC1**): Verify `buildFactoryState` retains merged PRs at 48h and 6d23h inside `lanes.merged_recent` (including carry-over from `prev` and token attachment), and drops merged PRs at >7d (e.g. 8 days before `now`).
- `UT-2` (**AC2**): Verify `updateHistory` default cap retains >72 snapshots (up to 500) and slices at 500 when `cfg.historyKeep` is omitted, and still trims to `cfg.historyKeep` when explicitly provided.
- `UT-3` (**AC3**): Verify `capHistory` / `nextHistory` keeps 50 transitions intact and caps at 100 when >100 transitions are accumulated.
- `REG-1` (**AC4**): `node js/unit-tests/test_factoryState.js` passes with zero failures.

## Non-goals
- Changing token ledger window (`DEFAULT_WINDOW_DAYS = 14` / `ROW_KEEP = 40` in `js/factory/token_usage.js` and `scripts/publish-token-usage.sh`) — out of scope for this issue.
- Deleting historical `data/<base>-<stamp>.json` files from the `factory-data` branch.

`historyPutCommand` emits the same `-f content="$(printf %s '<json>' | base64)"`

(~197B/entry). Rebuilt exactly as `updateHistory` writes it:

`keep`), so ~1.7 days in (at the 5-min cadence this ticket assumes; ~3.5d at

freezes just short of the depth this ticket bought.

(~80 KB)"* — that assumption is empirically false: with real URL/stamp shapes
the 500-entry index is 98.6KB, past the measured break.

add a REG test asserting the built index stays under the ceiling — or fix the
transport (temp file + `gh api --input`), which lifts the ceiling for the

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1151._

> ℹ️ **1 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `js/factoryState.js` line 185

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-21):
🚨 **BLOCKING: the 7d window × the 100-PR merged feed pushes the state snapshot past the executor's command-size ceiling — `publishFactoryState` fails on every tick, board silently goes stale**

`github_list_prs state:'merged'` (the `mergedPrs` producer, `js/common/smProvider.js:265-273`) returns a page of **100 merged PRs**. For this repo right now that page spans only **4.4 days** of merges (~23/day): 4 of those PRs fall inside the current 24h window, but **all 100 fall inside the new 7d window**. `merged_recent` therefore grows from ~4-8 cards to 100 cards on every tick.

I built the state with the live 100-PR feed through the real `buildFactoryState` (real titles/refs, realistic carried stamps, 6-entry histories, `checks`, `tokens` rows — the fields `mergedPrCard`/`carryTimestamps`/`mergedChecksFor` produce):

```
24h window (today):  8 cards  → state JSON     4,818B
7d window (this PR): 100 cards → state JSON 104,489B  ❌
```

**104,489B is past the hard transport ceiling.** `snapshotPutCommand` emits
`gh api -X PUT … -f content="$(printf %s '<json>' | base64)"`. I probed this
exact command shape on the installed dmtools binary (`cli_execute_command`):
the base64-expanded content becomes a single `execve` argument, and Linux
`MAX_ARG_STRLEN` (131,072B) kills it — bisected break point at **~96.7KB of
JSON payload** (96,752B passes, 97,632B fails with exit 126 `Argument list
too long`). Today's state (~5-20KB) is far under it; this PR crosses it
deterministically at the current merge rate.

Failure mode is silent: `js/smAgent.js:5537-5541` catches the throw and only
logs `⚠️ factory state publish failed` — the tick stays green while the board
stops updating (state, mutex, rework-latch, alarms persistence all ride this
snapshot).

Suggested directions (any one):
- Cap the lane like `BACKLOG_CAP` (`js/factoryState.js:1006-1008` precedent): keep the 7d semantics, `.slice(0, MERGED_LANE_CAP)` the newest ~40-50 cards.
- Thin merged-card payloads (drop `checks`/`tokens`/history bulk for terminal cards).
- Fix the transport (temp file + `gh api --input`), which lifts the ceiling for both this and the history index.

Either way, please add a REG guard asserting the built state JSON stays under the measured ceiling, so this can't regress silently.

---

### Thread 2 — `js/factoryState.js` line 207

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-21):
🚨 **BLOCKING: HISTORY_KEEP=500 builds a history index that deterministically exceeds the executor's command-size ceiling — `updateHistory` fails permanently once the index fills**

`historyPutCommand` emits the same `-f content="$(printf %s '<json>' | base64)"`
shape as the state PUT, so the index JSON rides a single `execve` argument
capped by Linux `MAX_ARG_STRLEN` (131,072B). I probed this exact shape on the
installed dmtools binary: **~96.7KB of JSON is the ceiling** (96,752B OK,
97,632B → exit 126 `Argument list too long`).

The index size is deterministic — every entry's `ts`/`tick` are ISO stamps and
`url` is `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/<repo>/<branch>/data/<base>-<stamp>.json`
(~197B/entry). Rebuilt exactly as `updateHistory` writes it:

```
keep= 72 (today): 14,265B  ✅
keep=465:          91,685B  ✅ (last safe point)
keep=500 (this PR):98,580B  ❌ over the ceiling
```

The index grows monotonically after rollout (one entry per tick, trimmed to
`keep`), so ~1.7 days in (at the 5-min cadence this ticket assumes; ~3.5d at
10-min) the PUT starts failing **on every subsequent tick forever**: the retry
re-reads the stuck index, unshifts one entry, trims to 500 — always over the
ceiling. `js/smAgent.js:5543-5549` swallows it as
`⚠️ factory state history failed`, so the board's time-travel slider silently
freezes just short of the depth this ticket bought.

Note the ticket itself justifies 500 with *"keeping JSON payload size small
(~80 KB)"* — that assumption is empirically false: with real URL/stamp shapes
the 500-entry index is 98.6KB, past the measured break.

Fix: bound the default to ≤ ~450 (ceiling ÷ ~197B/entry, with headroom) and
add a REG test asserting the built index stays under the ceiling — or fix the
transport (temp file + `gh api --input`), which lifts the ceiling for the
state snapshot too.

---

### Thread 3 — `js/factoryState.js` line 260

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-21):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the "~4h" eviction math in this comment is now stale — it was computed for the old `HISTORY_CAP = 24`**

The guard this comment documents is unchanged, but the number below it no
longer follows from the constants this PR edits: without the dedupe guard,
each tick appends a duplicate terminal entry and the cap starts evicting the
real timeline after `HISTORY_CAP` ticks. At the new `HISTORY_CAP = 100` that
is **~16.7h at the 10-min cadence** (~8.3h at 5-min), not "~4h" (which is
24 × 10min, the old cap).

One-line comment fix so the motivation quoted in `test_factoryState.js:563-565`
and the code stay in sync.

---

### Thread 4 — `js/unit-tests/test_factoryState.js` line 1133

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-21):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the AC2 test re-implements the exec-mock scaffolding of the neighboring index test — extract a small helper**

`gh-1150 AC2` (this test) and `updateHistory: existing index — append, carry
sha, trim to keep` (js/unit-tests/test_factoryState.js:1101-1130) duplicate the
same ~15-line mock: probe `--jq .sha` → `'feedface'`, probe `--jq .content` →
`JSON.stringify(old)`, then fish the last PUT out of `seen` and regex-extract
`"url":"…"` pairs. A tiny helper, e.g.

```js
function withHistoryIndex(snaps, run) {
  var seen = [];
  fsModule.updateHistory(ST,
    { repo: 'IstiN/flutter_agent_harness', asset: 'fa-state.json', historyKeep: snaps.keep },
    function (a) {
      seen.push(a.command);
      if (a.command.indexOf('--jq .sha') > 0) return { output: 'feedface\n' };
      if (a.command.indexOf('--jq .content') > 0) return { output: JSON.stringify(snaps.old) };
      return undefined;
    });
  run(seen);

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1151._

> ℹ️ **1 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `js/factoryState.js` line 185

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-21):
🚨 **BLOCKING: the 7d window × the 100-PR merged feed pushes the state snapshot past the executor's command-size ceiling — `publishFactoryState` fails on every tick, board silently goes stale**

`github_list_prs state:'merged'` (the `mergedPrs` producer, `js/common/smProvider.js:265-273`) returns a page of **100 merged PRs**. For this repo right now that page spans only **4.4 days** of merges (~23/day): 4 of those PRs fall inside the current 24h window, but **all 100 fall inside the new 7d window**. `merged_recent` therefore grows from ~4-8 cards to 100 cards on every tick.

I built the state with the live 100-PR feed through the real `buildFactoryState` (real titles/refs, realistic carried stamps, 6-entry histories, `checks`, `tokens` rows — the fields `mergedPrCard`/`carryTimestamps`/`mergedChecksFor` produce):

```
24h window (today):  8 cards  → state JSON     4,818B
7d window (this PR): 100 cards → state JSON 104,489B  ❌
```

**104,489B is past the hard transport ceiling.** `snapshotPutCommand` emits
`gh api -X PUT … -f content="$(printf %s '<json>' | base64)"`. I probed this
exact command shape on the installed dmtools binary (`cli_execute_command`):
the base64-expanded content becomes a single `execve` argument, and Linux
`MAX_ARG_STRLEN` (131,072B) kills it — bisected break point at **~96.7KB of
JSON payload** (96,752B passes, 97,632B fails with exit 126 `Argument list
too long`). Today's state (~5-20KB) is far under it; this PR crosses it
deterministically at the current merge rate.

Failure mode is silent: `js/smAgent.js:5537-5541` catches the throw and only
logs `⚠️ factory state publish failed` — the tick stays green while the board
stops updating (state, mutex, rework-latch, alarms persistence all ride this
snapshot).

Suggested directions (any one):
- Cap the lane like `BACKLOG_CAP` (`js/factoryState.js:1006-1008` precedent): keep the 7d semantics, `.slice(0, MERGED_LANE_CAP)` the newest ~40-50 cards.
- Thin merged-card payloads (drop `checks`/`tokens`/history bulk for terminal cards).
- Fix the transport (temp file + `gh api --input`), which lifts the ceiling for both this and the history index.

Either way, please add a REG guard asserting the built state JSON stays under the measured ceiling, so this can't regress silently.

---

### Thread 2 — `js/factoryState.js` line 207

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-21):
🚨 **BLOCKING: HISTORY_KEEP=500 builds a history index that deterministically exceeds the executor's command-size ceiling — `updateHistory` fails permanently once the index fills**

`historyPutCommand` emits the same `-f content="$(printf %s '<json>' | base64)"`
shape as the state PUT, so the index JSON rides a single `execve` argument
capped by Linux `MAX_ARG_STRLEN` (131,072B). I probed this exact shape on the
installed dmtools binary: **~96.7KB of JSON is the ceiling** (96,752B OK,
97,632B → exit 126 `Argument list too long`).

The index size is deterministic — every entry's `ts`/`tick` are ISO stamps and
`url` is `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/<repo>/<branch>/data/<base>-<stamp>.json`
(~197B/entry). Rebuilt exactly as `updateHistory` writes it:

```
keep= 72 (today): 14,265B  ✅
keep=465:          91,685B  ✅ (last safe point)
keep=500 (this PR):98,580B  ❌ over the ceiling
```

The index grows monotonically after rollout (one entry per tick, trimmed to
`keep`), so ~1.7 days in (at the 5-min cadence this ticket assumes; ~3.5d at
10-min) the PUT starts failing **on every subsequent tick forever**: the retry
re-reads the stuck index, unshifts one entry, trims to 500 — always over the
ceiling. `js/smAgent.js:5543-5549` swallows it as
`⚠️ factory state history failed`, so the board's time-travel slider silently
freezes just short of the depth this ticket bought.

Note the ticket itself justifies 500 with *"keeping JSON payload size small
(~80 KB)"* — that assumption is empirically false: with real URL/stamp shapes
the 500-entry index is 98.6KB, past the measured break.

Fix: bound the default to ≤ ~450 (ceiling ÷ ~197B/entry, with headroom) and
add a REG test asserting the built index stays under the ceiling — or fix the
transport (temp file + `gh api --input`), which lifts the ceiling for the
state snapshot too.

---

### Thread 3 — `js/factoryState.js` line 260

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-21):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the "~4h" eviction math in this comment is now stale — it was computed for the old `HISTORY_CAP = 24`**

The guard this comment documents is unchanged, but the number below it no
longer follows from the constants this PR edits: without the dedupe guard,
each tick appends a duplicate terminal entry and the cap starts evicting the
real timeline after `HISTORY_CAP` ticks. At the new `HISTORY_CAP = 100` that
is **~16.7h at the 10-min cadence** (~8.3h at 5-min), not "~4h" (which is
24 × 10min, the old cap).

One-line comment fix so the motivation quoted in `test_factoryState.js:563-565`
and the code stay in sync.

---

### Thread 4 — `js/unit-tests/test_factoryState.js` line 1133

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-21):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the AC2 test re-implements the exec-mock scaffolding of the neighboring index test — extract a small helper**

`gh-1150 AC2` (this test) and `updateHistory: existing index — append, carry
sha, trim to keep` (js/unit-tests/test_factoryState.js:1101-1130) duplicate the
same ~15-line mock: probe `--jq .sha` → `'feedface'`, probe `--jq .content` →
`JSON.stringify(old)`, then fish the last PUT out of `seen` and regex-extract
`"url":"…"` pairs. A tiny helper, e.g.

```js
function withHistoryIndex(snaps, run) {
  var seen = [];
  fsModule.updateHistory(ST,
    { repo: 'IstiN/flutter_agent_harness', asset: 'fa-state.json', historyKeep: snaps.keep },
    function (a) {
      seen.push(a.command);
      if (a.command.indexOf('--jq .sha') > 0) return { output: 'feedface\n' };
      if (a.command.indexOf('--jq .content') > 0) return { output: JSON.stringify(snaps.old) };
      return undefined;
    });
  run(seen);
}
```

keeps the third future variant cheap. Optional polish — the duplication is
small and both tests read fine as written.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1151
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1151
- **Title**: feat(factoryState): extend MERGED_WINDOW_MS to 7d, HISTORY_KEEP to 500, and HISTORY_CAP to 100 (gh-1150)
- **Author**: IstiN
- **Branch**: `feat/gh-1150-state-retention` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +110
- **Deletions**: -24
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T20:19:40Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-21T20:41:11Z

## PR Description

## Summary

Implements **gh-1150** — extends factory state retention and card lifecycle history caps in `js/factoryState.js`:

- **`MERGED_WINDOW_MS`**: `7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000` (7 days, up from 24h) so merged PR cards and their accumulated lifecycle timestamps (`reviewedAt`, `approvedAt`, `validatingAt`), `card.history`, and `card.tokens` remain in `lanes.merged_recent` for a full week.
- **`HISTORY_KEEP`**: `500` (up from 72) so `updateHistory()` keeps up to 500 snapshots in `data/<base>-history.json` by default (~41h at 5m cadence / ~83h at 10m cadence), while preserving explicit `cfg.historyKeep` overrides.
- **`HISTORY_CAP`**: `100` (up from 24) so `capHistory()` retains up to 100 per-card state transitions in `card.history`.

## Verification

- `node js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js js/unit-tests/test_factoryState.js` — 173 passed, 0 failed (`UT-1`, `UT-2`, `UT-3`, `REG-1`).
- `node js/agentDocGenerator.js && git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated` — clean.

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: HISTORY_KEEP=500 builds a history index that deterministically exceeds the executor's command-size ceiling — `updateHistory` fails permanently once the index fills**

`historyPutCommand` emits the same `-f content="$(printf %s '<json>' | base64)"`

The index size is deterministic — every entry's `ts`/`tick` are ISO stamps and
`url` is `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/<repo>/<branch>/data/<base>-<stamp>.json`
(~197B/entry). Rebuilt exactly as `updateHistory` writes it:

```
keep= 72 (today): 14,265B  ✅
keep=465:          91,685B  ✅ (last safe point)
keep=500 (this PR):98,580B  ❌ over the ceiling
```

The index grows monotonically after rollout (one entry per tick, trimmed to
`keep`), so ~1.7 days in (at the 5-min cadence this ticket assumes; ~3.5d at
10-min) the PUT starts failing **on every subsequent tick forever**: the retry
re-reads the stuck index, unshifts one entry, trims to 500 — always over the
ceiling. `js/smAgent.js:5543-5549` swallows it as
`⚠️ factory state history failed`, so the board's time-travel slider silently
freezes just short of the depth this ticket bought.

(~80 KB)"* — that assumption is empirically false: with real URL/stamp shapes
the 500-entry index is 98.6KB, past the measured break.

Fix: bound the default to ≤ ~450 (ceiling ÷ ~197B/entry, with headroom) and
add a REG test asserting the built index stays under the ceiling — or fix the
transport (temp file + `gh api --input`), which lifts the ceiling for the
state snapshot too.

shape as the state PUT, so the index JSON rides a single `execve` argument

installed dmtools binary: **~96.7KB of JSON is the ceiling** (96,752B OK,

The index grows monotonically after rollout (one entry per tick, trimmed to

Implements **gh-1150** — extends factory state retention and card lifecycle history caps in `js/factoryState.js`:

Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone.
